newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French December bond futures were buoyed late in the session by rallies in the German and U.S. bond markets to post a new contract closing high.

A weaker-than-expected U.S. National Association of Purchasing Managers survey sent the December contract to 125.10, just shy of the intra-day contract high at 125.14, and it settled at 125.08. The previous closing high was 124.84.

The contract continued to climb in the GLOBEX session, reaching a high of 125.16. Traders said there was a risk of profit taking at these levels although the market would be relatively well supported by domestic demand.
"It's been a pretty one-way market. I've been bullish up to now but we're nearing levels for profit-taking," said Valerie Plagnol, economist at Credit Commercial de France.

An analyst at a French brokerage said, however, "Even if we get some bad news, the French market should not fall that much because of the liquidity coming into the market when the BTAN matures in the middle of October."
The outstanding volume of the 6.50 percent 1996 BTAN, which matures on October 12, is 65.2 billion francs.
The Treasury announced it would sell between 16 and 18 billion francs of OATs, in three lines, at Thursday's auction.

It will be selling the TEC 10 variable rate OAT and the April 2011 OAT in addition to the current 10-year benchmark, the October 2006 OAT. Analysts had expected a combination of these three bonds to be on offer.
Traders said volume would probably be split evenly between the three bonds and that overall the sale would not pose any problems for the market even at these high levels.

They said the TEC 10 was still in demand and the 2011 OAT, created earlier this year in response to domestic demand, should also be sold relatively easily given the recent interest in longer-dated bonds.

More unions joined the call for a one-day strike on October 17 today but analysts said at the moment there was still nothing to suggest any social unrest would threaten the government's resolve or ability to enforce its budget measures.

"The government has the means, the ways and the weapons to put the budget through the way it wants," said Plagnol at CCF. "To make the risks realities you first need a union of unions and then you need a translation of this movement into a political debate within the government."
Unions representing gas and utility workers called for a walkout on October 17, a day set for civil service strikes.
The 10-year spread over Bunds widened slightly on Tuesday to three basis points from one on Monday.

The franc weakened against the mark late in the session and was trading at 3.3875 at 1600 GMT, the lowest level since September 24, compared with 3.3853 late on Monday and the high for the week at 3.3804.
Call money remained unchanged at 3-3/8 1/2 percent, disappointing some hopes that the Bank of France would continue to steer the overnight rate lower, analysts said.
